{"content": "### Verify a container with OIDC

Source: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/README.md

Verifies an image by specifying the expected certificate identity and OIDC issuer.

```shell
cosign verify $IMAGE --certificate-identity=$IDENTITY --certificate-oidc-issuer=$OIDC_ISSUER
```

--------------------------------

### Attaching Attestation with Certificate Chain

Source: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/doc/cosign_attest.md

Attaches an attestation to a container image using a local key pair, including a certificate and certificate chain.

```bash
cosign attest --predicate <FILE> --type <TYPE> --key cosign.key --cert cosign.crt --cert-chain chain.crt <IMAGE>
```

### cosign_attest-blob.md

Source: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/doc/cosign_attest-blob.md

The `attest-blob` command allows for specifying the predicate type, which can be one of several predefined formats like `slsaprovenance`, `spdx`, `cyclonedx`, or a custom URI. It also supports writing verification materials to a bundle file and can accept attestation data via standard input.

--------------------------------

### cosign verify-attestation

Source: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/doc/cosign_verify-attestation.md

For keyless verification flows, you must specify either `--certificate-identity` or `--certificate-identity-regexp` to define the expected identity in a Fulcio certificate. You also need to specify either `--certificate-oidc-issuer` or `--certificate-oidc-issuer-regexp` to define the expected OIDC issuer.

--------------------------------

### cosign verify

Source: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/main/doc/cosign_verify.md

For keyless verification flows, you can specify expected certificate identity using `--certificate-identity` or a regular expression with `--certificate-identity-regexp`. Similarly, the OIDC issuer can be specified with `--certificate-oidc-issuer` or `--certificate-oidc-issuer-regexp`.", "results": []}
